requirements.requirement: node1 hands out addresses on the private network shared with node2 and node3
requirements.summary: node1's eth1 was brought up and configured as a new 'priv' static interface (192.168.50.1/24), added to the lan firewall zone, and dnsmasq was configured with a DHCP pool (192.168.50.100-150) on that interface. Both node2 and node3 successfully obtained DHCP leases from node1 via dhclient, confirmed by DHCPOFFER/DHCPACK exchanges and node1's lease file.

requirements.requirement: node2 always receives the same address across repeated leases
requirements.summary: A static DHCP host reservation was added for node2's eth1 MAC (02:9b:00:10:4b:23) mapping to 192.168.50.50. This was confirmed across an initial lease, an explicit release/renew cycle, and again after a full node1+node2 restart cycle — node2 consistently received 192.168.50.50 each time, and node1's lease file reflects the named reservation.

requirements.requirement: node3 is addressed from the general pool
requirements.summary: node3 has no static reservation and obtained 192.168.50.103, a pool address within the configured range 100-150, confirmed via dhclient output and node1's lease file, including after a full restart cycle.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task are directly and coherently evidenced: node1 now serves DHCP on the shared private network (192.168.50.0/24) via a newly created 'priv' interface and dnsmasq pool, node2 has a MAC-keyed static reservation confirmed stable across repeated release/renew and a full restart, and node3 draws from the general pool and is confirmed stable across a restart as well. The executor also ran the independent node-restart protocol on all three nodes with full pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data state, which the fixed lifecycle snapshots corroborate.
limitations: Package-health checks for node2 and node3 timed out both before and after the executor's work (status 'unavailable'), so package-manager state on the RHEL nodes could not be independently cross-checked, though this is unrelated to the DHCP task outcomes.

node1's OpenWrt 'platform' observation failed post-restart due to an SSH connection reset (return_code 255), so the after_executor OS-release snapshot for node1 is missing; boot-identity and service state were still directly confirmed via executor commands.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed the chronological command trace: all state-changing commands (bringing up eth1, creating the 'priv' UCI network interface, adding it to the lan firewall zone, configuring dhcp.priv and the node2 host reservation, restarting network/firewall/dnsmasq services, and the dhclient release/renew/reboot cycles on node2/node3) map directly to satisfying the three material requirements or to the independent restart-evidence protocol. Two early attempts to schedule a background reboot on node1 failed harmlessly ('disown: not found', 'nohup: not found', cmd-af9b0c569dfb41dd, cmd-ef1ddb90f4f649be) with no state change before the working reboot command succeeded (cmd-fa33ede4d4d14c42). No abandoned residue, conflicting services, unnecessary mutations, or weakened security controls were found; the lifecycle diff shows only expected artifacts (dnsmasq lease/state files, reboot logs, transient systemd-private dirs).
